title: Fastpath review playbook & anchoring notes
content:
Quick context:
- Scratchpad for one-hour fastpath PR reviews; aim: minimal changes with safe rollout.
- Working against PR-4382 (batching scheduler refactor). goal is to keep throughput improvements without regressions.

Notes to self (high level):
- Prioritize: correctness, perf regressions, observable instrumentation, and rollback plan.
- If something feels risky (deep data model changes, cross-cutting config), stop and request a follow-up PR.

Heuristics / checklist (fast):
1) Compile & smoke run locally + docker image build (10m)
   - ./gradlew :serving:assemble && docker build -t local/serving:test .
2) Run unit tests for touched packages only (use --tests): 5-15m
3) Search for non-transitive dependency additions (native lib, kernel changes)
4) Look for hidden config gates or new feature flags that default to ON
5) Quick perf sanity: run a 1-min synthetic with baseline inputs, compare p50/p95. If p95 regresses >10% flag it.
6) Tracing: ensure new spans have names and are not high-cardinality (no raw request ids).
7) Ensure metrics emitted (counters/histograms) have unit tags and are in metrics registry file.

Risk mapping (quick matrix):
- Low risk: refactor local helper functions, variable renames, tests added/updated. Accept in fastpath.
- Medium risk: scheduler tweaks, batching thresholds, fallback logic. Require canary and perf baseline.
- High risk: KV cache format bump, RPC change, model-serving protocol change. Block fastpath; propose staged rollout.

Refactor idea seeds (notes to follow up later):
- Extract a small scheduler-adapter interface to avoid conditional logic on hardware type. Quick sketch:
  interface SchedulerAdapter {
    fun enqueue(req: InferenceRequest): EnqueueResult
    fun flush(): List<Batch>
  }
  // Benefit: isolates gpu-specific heuristics and simplifies unit tests.
- Move batch-eviction policy to config feature with default; add telemetry when eviction happens.
- Replace magic constants for max-concurrent-requests with named config object plus validation on startup.

Tests to add (minimal set for fastpath acceptance):
- Unit: scheduler enqueue/dequeue edge cases (empty batch, single-item flush).
- Integration: run small end-to-end with mocked KV cache to ensure cache hits preserved.
- Perf test: synthetic 1000 req spike, record p50/p95 token latency.

PR comments / suggested wording (copy-paste):
- "Nice cleanup — one request: add a short integration test covering the single-item flush path and a perf run snapshot in PR description so we can compare p95 before/after."
- "Why is pollInterval set to 5ms here? Can we make it configurable or add a short comment explaining choice?"
- "The new metrics look useful — please add the metric names to observability/metrics-index and include expected cardinality (low/medium/high)."

Observability & rollout plan (if merged to main):
- Canary: enable on dedicated pool 2 (10% traffic) for 24 hours.
- Alerts: spike in p95 > 1.1x baseline OR error-rate increase > 0.5% -> auto-failover to previous scheduler.
- Logging: add structured log event when fallback occurs (reason + sample request id masked).

Open questions / uncertainties to resolve in follow-up PRs:
- Is the batching window compatible with latency-sensitive endpoints? (need product input: product/hosted-api)
- Are there any GPU driver requirements for the new kernel selection logic? (check infra ticket RED-3421)

Todo / next actions (assignments):
- Samir: add the single-item flush integration test and attach perf snapshot to PR (due: +2 days).
- Hana: validate new metrics and add to metrics-index (due: +3 days).
- Me (Ritika): run a manual canary with 10% traffic on sandbox and capture traces (due: before merge).

Notes to self (meta):
- Keep comments concise in PR; avoid over-commenting trivial lines. Use linked artifacts to point to tests and perf runs.
- If reviewer fatigue shows (multiple big comments), recommend splitting into two PRs: "refactor" (no behavior change) and "behavioral change" (with canary).

Random scratch items:
- Slack threads to ping: #eng-serving-runtime, @oncall-sre for canary window.
- Snippet to run perf: 
  python infra/tools/perf_run.py --workload small-spike --duration 60 --out perf-ritika.json
- Command to rollback a canary: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts/rollback?pool=dedicated-2

End of scratchpad.
